title: stable SLA window and compact scale-down planner
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: scale-down churn in Dedicated fleets can cause transient SLA regressions when many nodes are reclaimed during brief low-utilization tails. This PR introduces a compact scale-down planner that reasons over a configurable sustained-SLA window and a compacting epoch model to make conservative, rollback-safe scale-down decisions. Summary: 1) controller/fleet/compact_planner: new controller that computes a compacted scale-down plan combining percentile utilization, recent eviction history and predicted headroom from warm pools; 2) controller/fleet/scale_down_executor: implements a two-phase drain (soft-drain then exclusive purge) with preemption-safe markers to avoid over-eviction; 3) telemetry: new metrics (fleet.sla_window_steady_pct, scale_down_confidence, compact_epoch_count) and dashboards for 5/50/95 utilization summaries aggregated per-tenant; 4) autoscaler integration: augments the existing autoscaler decision path to consult compact_planner when the requested delta is > 8% of fleet capacity; 5) safety: rollback hooks and a dry-run mode to emit only proposed actions for 24h before applying. Backwards compatibility: defaults are off for Dedicated clusters older than 2026-01 images and controlled via feature flag fleet.compact_scale_down.enabled. Testing: unit tests for planning logic, integration tests in benchmark-lab that replay week-long telemetry traces, and an e2e that validates no increase in tail latency on canary cluster. Performance impact: planner evaluation is O(N) over shard summaries (N = number of allocation shards) and runs every 60s by default; CPU/memory overhead measured at <1% for 1k-shard fleets in our perf-canary. Rollout: feature gated, gradual ramp to 25% of Dedicated fleets, automatic fallback to conservative decider if scale_down_confidence < 0.6. Related: ENG-1982 (reduce SLA blips on scale-down) and SUP-7421 (customer incident describing thrash during nightly backfills).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Can we make the default window configurable per-tenant? Response: yes, added tenant_window_override and validated fallbacks in the planner, see compact_planner.go lines 142-168.

Priya Nair: The rollback hook needs a circuit-breaker to avoid repeated re-invokes. Response: added circuit state backed by a short-lived annotation; executor will refuse to reapply rollback more than 3x in 10m.
Luca Romano: telemetry cardinality looks high for per-tenant 1s histograms. Response: switched to 1m rollups and pre-aggregation in metrics/recorders, reduced cardinality by ~12x.
release_notes: Introduced 'compact scale-down planner' for Dedicated fleets: safer, confidence-driven scale-downs that reduce SLA blips during capacity reduction. Feature-gated and disabled by default for older images. Metrics: fleet.sla_window_steady_pct, scale_down_confidence. Rollout will be gradual with dry-run option.
notes_for_operators: Operators: to enable on a cluster set feature flag fleet.compact_scale_down.enabled=true and optionally fleet.compact_scale_down.window_minutes and max_epoch_compaction in cluster config. Monitor fleet.sla_window_steady_pct and scale_down_confidence; if confidence stays low for >1h, the planner will revert to the legacy decider automatically.
hotfix_related_incident: SUP-7421 (customer reported repeated eviction spikes during nightly maintenance)
